caption: A scoop of sorbet is set on a waffle fresh off the iron, and it slumps and runs into the squares.

sa.check: A scoop of sorbet sits on a waffle.
Coloured liquid fills the waffle's squares.
Liquid runs off the waffle's edge.
The waffle is fresh off the iron.
The softening comes first and the running follows.

pc.expect: The scoop only softens, sinks and shrinks while the liquid spreads; it does not firm up again on the hot waffle.
pc.fail: The scoop regains a firm round shape; or the liquid draws back into the scoop; or the sorbet freezes hard again on the hot waffle; or the scoop alternates between firmer and softer.

pc.expect: The melt runs downward into the waffle's squares, fills them and runs off its lowest edge.
pc.fail: The melt climbs out of a square and over a ridge uphill; or the liquid gathers on the waffle's ridges and stays; or a drip leaves the waffle and rises; or the melt runs up the scoop's side.

pc.expect: The sorbet is a soft wet solid that slumps and sheds a thin coloured liquid, and the waffle stays a crisp grid that softens only where soaked.
pc.fail: The waffle melts or sags with the sorbet; or the melt runs as a thick paste that keeps ridges; or the scoop shatters into dry crumbs; or the melt sets into a spike standing out from the waffle.

pc.expect: The melt comes from the softening scoop and wets what it passes: the waffle darkens where the liquid runs.
pc.fail: Liquid fills the squares while the scoop above stays hard-edged and dry; or the waffle stays dry where liquid has run; or liquid appears in a square with none running into it.

pc.expect: One scoop on one waffle; the sorbet goes only from the scoop into the squares and off the edge.
pc.fail: The scoop grows; or a second scoop appears; or the scoop vanishes while still whole; or liquid appears on the plate with none running off the waffle.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The sorbet's colour, the waffle's pattern and the plate stay the same.
pc.fail: The sorbet changes colour; or the waffle's grid changes pattern; or the plate changes shape.
